ai.description: This frog reaches 30–40 mm. It is brown with a pale vertebral stripe and dark limb bars. Distinctive features include a pointed snout and reduced toe webbing that does not reach the discs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Minervarya brevipalmata* is best distinguished by its significantly reduced toe webbing, which does not extend beyond the basal segments of the digits.
ai.habitat: *Minervarya brevipalmata* inhabits moist deciduous forests and evergreen forest floors, typically found near water bodies at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Short-webbed Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates among leaf litter and damp vegetation near water bodies.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Minervarya brevipalmata* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of pigmented eggs in shallow pools or water-filled depressions.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Minervarya brevipalmata* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala, Karnataka, and Maharashtra at low to moderate elevations.
ai.callDescription: The call of *Minervarya brevipalmata* consists of a series of rapid, high-pitched metallic chirps, typically heard emanating from temporary rain pools and flooded grasslands.
